feeds.title: MGH Center for Women's Mental Health Blog
feeds.description: MGH is the Center for Women's Mental Health provides state-of-the-art evaluation & treatment of psychiatric disorders associated with female reproductive functions. The blog post covers a range of topics including ADHD, Anxiety Disorders, Maternal Depression, PMDD, Depression in Women, Pregnancy, Miscarriage, and Mental Health.

feeds.title: Therapy for Black Girls Blog
feeds.description: The Therapy for Black Girls podcast is a weekly conversation with Dr. Joy Harden Bradford, a licensed psychologist in Atlanta, Georgia, about all things mental health, personal development, and all the small decisions we can make to become the best possible version of ourselves.

feeds.title: Sanity Daily Blog
feeds.description: Priyanka Joshi is a top mental health blogger, dedicated to helping individuals achieve optimal mental health and well-being. Her blog Sanity Daily is all about providing practical tips, insights, and evidence-based strategies to help individuals improve their mental health and well-being. Explore more mental health issues and challenges in new posts.

feeds.title: Natasha Tracy Blog
feeds.description: This bipolar blog talks about mental illness, mental health and more. Natasha Tracy is a bipolar expert, speaker, author, and person living with bipolar disorder.

feeds.title: Be Your Own Light
feeds.description: This blog is written by Eleanor Segall. Diagnosed with bipolar 1 disorder (a mood disorder) at 16, and now in her twenties, she blogs about what has helped her in recovery and tries to help others too.

feeds.title: Jennifer Marshall Blog
feeds.description: Jennifer Marshal writes about living with bipolar and mental illness through her blog and openly talks with her kids about mental health.

feeds.title: What WayD Says Blog
feeds.description: A mental health blog by Waheeda Joosab with a primary focus on the mental health issues that affect women in general, and parents and teachers in particular, and a secondary focus on hobbies for mental health.

feeds.title: The DV Walking Wounded Blog
feeds.description: The Walking Wounded is just an inspirational page for survivors of domestic and sexual abuse. This page is for survivors and victims alike, as well as their support squad - we pray and are working toward a world without abuse of ANY kind.

feeds.title: Ashley Clark Comegys Blog
feeds.description: Covers articles on mental health, trauma, anxiety, depression, stress, grief and much more. Ashley helps women deal with the challenges of life by helping them achieve balance in their day to day activities.

feeds.title: The Bipolar Buzz Blog
feeds.description: Alaina Raquel is a Ph.D. dropout living with Bipolar disorder and anxiety. Through this blog, she talks about her mental health journey and recovery.

feeds.title: My 12 Steps Closer to God
feeds.description: Destiny Woman of Faith is a personal blog dedicated to mental health recovery through faith. The author shares her journey of overcoming PTSD, depression, anxiety, and codependency by following a 12-step program rooted in spirituality and support. The site provides insights into recognizing symptoms, seeking help, and the transformative power of God's grace. The author encourages readers to find professional help and offers her book as a resource for those facing similar struggles.

feeds.title: Bevoya Blog
feeds.description: An in-depth blog with personal stories about how stress, anxiety, and overthinking affects people in everyday life. These stories help people experiencing physical symptoms (like migraines) as a result the chaotic pace of life. The site Beautiful Voyager was founded by Meredith for overthinkers, people-pleasers, and perfectionists.

feeds.title: IVY'S PPD Blog
feeds.description: Covers articles on maternal mental health, postpartum depression, postpartum mood disorder, perinatal depression, and more. Author Ivy Shih Leung is a PPD survivor and always looks for opportunities to raise public awareness.

feeds.title: Ellen's OCD Blog
feeds.description: Hello! My name is Ellen and I'm 22. I have OCD and I blog about my experiences with it, hopefully helping other's along the way.

feeds.title: Becoming Indomitable
feeds.description: The site shares my story and how I was able to overcome each tragedy in my life and also shares free resources like CBT and DBT worksheets, coping skills, and other tools to help people get back on their feet. I grew up without a support system and had a ton of setbacks in my life. I really want to help those who may be going through the same thing see the path forward and know how to get over their trauma and have a better life so they may become indomitable too.

feeds.title: The Anarchist Soccer Mom
feeds.description: Liza is a writer, educator, and mental health advocate who writes and features mental health stories from her perspective as a mom.

feeds.title: Bipolar Bandit
feeds.description: The blog covers topics on bipolar disorder, mental illnesses, mental health advocacy, and more. Michelle was diagnosed with bipolar disorder 35 yrs ago and hopes to educate, offer hope and inspire readers through her blog.

feeds.title: Anxious Lass » Mental Health
feeds.description: Anxious Lass is a lifestyle & mental health blog, where Kelly speaks candidly about mental health, chronic illness, and the general ups and downs of life.

feeds.title: HealthyPlace » Coping With Depression
feeds.description: Articles include tips for managing depression, experiences with depression treatments and different aspects of coping with depression. At HealthyPlace, you'll find comprehensive, authoritative information on psychological disorders, psychiatric medications, and other mental health treatments.

feeds.title: Alison Dotson Blog
feeds.description: The website is a plethora of resources that will help anyone to turn the tables on OCD. Allison is an active member in providing helpful resources to those who also suffered from OCD.

feeds.title: My OCD Coach Blog
feeds.description: Danielle is a Certified Life Coach and OCD Specialist who's recovered from OCD (and anxiety/depression) and now helps others get to the full recovery stage as well.
